title: Facilitators are generally barred from engaging with counterparties at all, and must document the exceptions
content:
A.1.7.8 states that "Facilitators are generally prohibited from engaging with counterparties," where counterparties means "external parties or entities with whom the Facilitators might interact in the context of governance operations, such as Ecosystem Actors (active or incubating)" (A.1.7.8.0.3.1). "The sole exception to this rule is where Facilitators must communicate with counterparties to set up governance processes. In such cases, the Facilitators must clearly detail their interactions."

The Action Tenet A.1.7.8.0.4.1 specifies what detailing means: "thoroughly document all aspects of their communications and dealings with counterparties. This includes the content of discussions, the context of interactions (date and time), and any decisions made or actions taken as a result."

Prohibiting contact rather than prohibiting *improper* contact is the notable choice. Improper influence is nearly impossible to detect after the fact — a facilitator who was persuaded in a private conversation looks the same as one who reasoned independently. Making contact itself the regulated act moves the enforcement question from "were you influenced?" (unprovable) to "did you meet, and did you log it?" (checkable). This is the same substitution of a formal test for a substantive one used in the single-role rule (A.1.5.5.0.4.1).

It also interlocks tightly with A.1.7.7. If a facilitator may only decide on publicly available information, then private conversations with the parties affected by their decisions are worse than useless — they generate exactly the internal knowledge the facilitator is forbidden to rely on. Barring the contact removes the temptation and the appearance together.

The cost is real friction: facilitators must operate at arm's length from the actors whose work they oversee, which forecloses informal problem-solving. A.1.7.9 accepts that cost explicitly, framing exhaustive documentation of "all interactions with ecosystem stakeholders" as an operational security requirement rather than administrative overhead.
description: A.1.7.8 permits contact only where necessary to set up governance processes; A.1.7.8.0.4.1 then requires recording content, date and time, and any resulting decisions or actions.
